record.bible_text: I <FI>am<Fi> the rose<WH02261> of Sharon<WH08289>, <FI>and<Fi> the lily<WH07799> of the valleys<WH06010>.
As the lily<WH07799> among thorns<WH02336>, so <FI>is<Fi> my love<WH07474> among the daughters<WH01323>.<CM>

As the apple tree<WH08598> among the trees<WH06086> of the wood<WH03293>, so <FI>is<Fi> my beloved<WH01730> among the sons<WH01121>. I sat<WH03427><WTH8804> down under his shadow<WH06738> with great delight<WH02530><WTH8765>, and his fruit<WH06529> <FI>was<Fi> sweet<WH04966> to my taste<WH02441>. <RF>I sat...: Heb. I delighted and sat down, etc<Rf> <RF>taste: Heb. palate<Rf>
He brought<WH0935><WTH8689> me to the banqueting<WH03196> house<WH01004>, and his banner<WH01714> over me <FI>was<Fi> love<WH0160>. <RF>banqueting...: Heb. house of wine<Rf>

Stay<WH05564><WTH8761> me with flagons<WH0809>, comfort<WH07502><WTH8761> me with apples<WH08598>: for I <FI>am<Fi> sick<WH02470><WTH8802> of love<WH0160>. <RF>comfort...: Heb. straw me with apples<Rf>
His left hand<WH08040> <FI>is<Fi> under my head<WH07218>, and his right hand<WH03225> doth embrace<WH02263><WTH8762> me.

I charge<WH07650><WTH8689> you, O ye daughters<WH01323> of Jerusalem<WH03389>, by the roes<WH06643>, and<WH0176> by the hinds<WH0355> of the field<WH07704>, that ye stir not up<WH05782><WTH8686>, nor awake<WH05782><WTH8787> <FI>my<Fi> love<WH0160>, till he please<WH02654><WTH8799>. <RF>I charge...: Heb. I adjure you<Rf><CM>
The voice<WH06963> of my beloved<WH01730>! behold, he cometh<WH0935><WTH8802> leaping<WH01801><WTH8764> upon the mountains<WH02022>, skipping<WH07092><WTH8764> upon the hills<WH01389>.

My beloved<WH01730> is like<WH01819><WTH8802> a roe<WH06643> or a young<WH06082> hart<WH0354>: behold, he standeth<WH05975><WTH8802> behind<WH0310> our wall<WH03796>, he looketh forth<WH07688><WTH8688> at the windows<WH02474>, shewing<WH06692><WTH8688> himself through the lattice<WH02762>. <RF>shewing...: Heb. flourishing<Rf>
My beloved<WH01730> spake<WH06030><WTH8804>, and said<WH0559><WTH8804> unto me, Rise up<WH06965><WTH8798>, my love<WH07474>, my fair one<WH03303>, and come away<WH03212><WTH8798>.
For, lo, the winter<WH05638> is past<WH05674><WTH8804>, the rain<WH01653> is over<WH02498><WTH8804> <FI>and<Fi> gone<WH01980><WTH8804>;

The flowers<WH05339> appear<WH07200><WTH8738> on the earth<WH0776>; the time<WH06256> of the singing<WH02158> <FI>of birds<Fi> is come<WH05060><WTH8689>, and the voice<WH06963> of the turtle<WH08449> is heard<WH08085><WTH8738> in our land<WH0776>;

The fig tree<WH08384> putteth forth<WH02590><WTH8804> her green figs<WH06291>, and the vines<WH01612> <FI>with<Fi> the tender grape<WH05563> give<WH05414><WTH8804> a <FI>good<Fi> smell<WH07381>. Arise<WH06965><WTH8798>, my love<WH07474>, my fair one<WH03303>, and come away<WH03212><WTH8798>.<CM>

O my dove<WH03123>, <FI>that art<Fi> in the clefts<WH02288> of the rock<WH05553>, in the secret<WH05643> <FI>places<Fi> of the stairs<WH04095>, let me see<WH07200><WTH8685> thy countenance<WH04758>, let me hear<WH08085><WTH8685> thy voice<WH06963>; for sweet<WH06156> <FI>is<Fi> thy voice<WH06963>, and thy countenance<WH04758> <FI>is<Fi> comely<WH05000>.
Take<WH0270><WTH8798> us the foxes<WH07776>, the little<WH06996> foxes<WH07776>, that spoil<WH02254><WTH8764> the vines<WH03754>: for our vines<WH03754> <FI>have<Fi> tender grapes<WH05563>.
My beloved<WH01730> <FI>is<Fi> mine, and I <FI>am<Fi> his: he feedeth<WH07462><WTH8802> among the lilies<WH07799>.

Until the day<WH03117> break<WH06315><WTH8799>, and the shadows<WH06752> flee away<WH05127><WTH8804>, turn<WH05437><WTH8798>, my beloved<WH01730>, and be thou like<WH01819><WTH8798> a roe<WH06643> or a young<WH06082> hart<WH0354> upon the mountains<WH02022> of Bether<WH01336>. <RF>of Bether: or, of division<Rf><CM>
